adversarial.evidence: wave run 2026-08-23 in the FALSE-NEGATIVE direction, which CLAUDE.md names as the one nobody runs: take genuinely vulnerable code and rename its identifiers to innocuous words. Four security plugins over the same file twice, `token`/`authToken` renamed to `dandelion`/`recipeDraft`. This rule was the only one of four whose finding disappeared — so the wave then attacked its own stated contract, that a value the code writes beats a guess about the key. It held in all three directions: a JWT literal reports under an innocuous key, under a credential-shaped key, AND when reached through a variable — the last of which the rule's comment never claimed. The disappearance is therefore an inherent limit, not a name-inference defect: `localStorage.setItem('recipeDraft', opaqueParam)` carries no evidence of a credential at all, which is L1/L2 rather than a wrong guess. No defect found. The contract was already locked by existing fixtures using JWT literals under the keys `flag`, `path`, `v` and `x`.
